newsitem.title: USA: NGC to sell off two-thirds of Destec assets.
newsitem.headline: NGC to sell off two-thirds of Destec assets.

text.p: NGC Corp expects to sell off about $300 million in non-strategic assets along with $407 million in international operations as part of its acquisition of Destec Energy Inc, executives said.
Houston-based NGC on Tuesday announced a $1.27 billion or $21.65 a share proposed acquisition of Destec in a deal company executives expect will receive "swift approval from federal regulators.
"It looks like a third of (Destec) is what we will end up with, and that's what we were interested in," NGC Chairman Chuck Watson said.

AES Corp would acquire Destec's international assets and operations, and NGC expects to consummate the previously announced $445 million sale of Destec's 220 megawatt Tiger Bay power plant to Florida Power Corp, NGC executives said.
NGC also plans to sell Destec's lignite and gas reserves and a coal gasification-synfuels plant, executives said.

After selling off the non-strategic assets to retire some of the interim financing used to acquire Destec, NGC's debt to capitalization ratio should fall back to the "mid-40s" from 55 percent, Watson said.

Destec is a Houston-based independent power producer with interests in 24 power projects with 5,136 megawatts of electricity, including major cogeneration facilities in Texas and California, the companies said.
"(The acquisition) really positons us to be an unquestioned leader in the deregulation of the electric business over the next several years," Watson said.
